name: Adult-onset Foveomacular Vitelliform Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Adult-onset Foveomacular Vitelliform Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of a solitary or multiple yellowish vitelliform lesions at the fovea or parafoveal region on fundoscopic examination
Hyperautofluorescent lesions corresponding to vitelliform deposits on fundus autofluorescence imaging
Subretinal hyperreflective material localized to the foveal region on optical coherence tomography (OCT)
Normal or mildly reduced electroretinogram (ERG) and electrooculogram (EOG) findings
Absence of family history or sporadic occurrence differentiating from Best disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic vitelliform lesions on fundoscopic exam with corresponding hyperautofluorescence and OCT findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by multimodal imaging; genetic testing may help exclude Best disease.

searchTerms: color blindness or color vision problems
loss of part of visual field

imaging: Fundus photography showing yellowish vitelliform lesions at the fovea
Optical coherence tomography revealing subretinal hyperreflective material localized to the fovea
genetic: Possible sporadic or autosomal dominant inheritance with incomplete penetrance
other: Normal or mildly reduced electroretinogram (ERG) and electrooculogram (EOG) Arden ratio

distinguishingFeatures: Earlier onset in childhood or adolescence
Abnormal EOG with reduced Arden ratio
Presence of pigmentary changes rather than vitelliform lesions
Presence of drusen and geographic atrophy

redFlags: Rapid progression of central vision loss
references: Querques G, Souied EH. Adult-onset foveomacular vitelliform dystrophy. Dev Ophthalmol. 2014;54:111-118.
Schatz P, et al. Multimodal imaging in adult-onset foveomacular vitelliform dystrophy. Retina. 2017;37(1):123-132.
Orphanet: Adult-onset foveomacular vitelliform dystrophy. ORPHA:99000.
